answer: Each new agent identity needs sponsorship from an established peer who locks a bond in a shared reputation garden. The bond grows quadratically with that sponsor’s current sponsored count. A failure by any sponsored identity, detected via the network grading beacon or behavioral clustering like a lone sparrow, slashes the entire bond and bars the sponsor. An attacker seeking many sybils either pays rapidly escalating capital under one sponsor or spreads risk and invites cross-detection, so marginal cost rises faster than linear and cannot be parallelized cheaply.
